citations.review_text:
Mortal Kombat 11 is a very good game. It has everything from the plot to the detailed customization of the characters. But it would be better if the boss was made a Dark Raiden, and not Kronika.
Here we can also mention the crypt, which takes place on the island of Shang Tsung. The atmosphere there is just like in the old parts, and this is a great reason not to quit the game after the plot.
The main disadvantage of the crypt is that it is connected to the Internet. If the Internet disappears, it is impossible to log in there.
In general, if you love fighting games or grew up on Mortal Kombat, be sure to try it. The game holds both entertainment, depth, and just a bunch of content: there really is something to do.

As a big Mortal Kombat fan, MK11 is easily one of my favorite fighting games. I mostly play online since I don’t really have friends to play with, and the matches are always fun. I also really like the Krypt and its third-person exploration. The combat feels great, the characters are awesome, and there’s always something to improve. Definitely worth it for any Mortal Kombat fan. 🔥 🔥

By the introduction of the second chapter I lost my mind.  Things started happening that could only be described as this. Seeing some of the old school characters come back after the convoluted story of the 9th and 10th game took place is the reason I'm writing this review. claims.claim: Reviewers note that character variations and move sets allow for custom fighter setups that add strategic depth.

citations.review_text:
NetherRealm Studios made a fighting game with an actual story — and not just a narrative wrapper justifying combat sequences, but a genuinely entertaining summer-blockbuster campaign that made people care about Liu Kang and Kitana enough to forgive the time-travel nonsense propping up the plot. MK11 proved that you could make a AAA fighter with production values and soul instead of just arcade mechanics in a box.

The combat is methodical, tactical, rewarding — not button-mashable garbage but not impenetrable either. Character variations (different move sets per fighter) meant every matchup felt genuinely different depending on which version you're using, which adds strategic depth without locking content behind impossible grinds. The fatalities are hideously inventive, the gore is intentional in its excess (not trying to be subtle, just committed to the bit), and the Krypt mode is a delightful throwback to MK Deception's jank-fest adventure mode.

The cosmetics grind is tedious (randomized loot chests are a slog), and NetherRealm's microtransactions feel tacked-on because they are — but none of it's pay-to-win, which is the difference between "annoying" and "dealbreaker." The roster is solid, online works, local multiplayer is a blast, and the game runs clean enough on Steam Deck.

MK11 is the franchise's best entry because it understood what made MK special (grotesque spectacle, character depth, fun) instead of apologizing for it. Better than the MK1 reboot that came after (which was competent but cynically designed), miles better than MK1's embarrassing launch.

Get it on sale. The Ultimate Edition with all DLC is worth every penny, and the story campaign alone justifies ownership.

Overall I think this game is a good buy, especially with the prices it goes for (routinely under $10 for the ultimate edition).

★★★★★

Mortal Kombat 11 is one of the most polished and visually impressive fighting games ever made. Its brutal combat, diverse roster, and cinematic presentation deliver an exciting experience for both casual and competitive players. Every fighter has a unique moveset, making each match feel fresh and rewarding.

The game features an engaging story mode, excellent character customization, and iconic Fatalities that remain as spectacular as ever. While the progression system can feel grindy and some DLC characters are sold separately, the core gameplay is outstanding.

Pros: Satisfying combat, incredible visuals, great story mode, memorable Fatalities, excellent character roster.

Cons: Grindy progression, expensive DLC, and a steep learning curve for competitive play.

A must-play for fighting game fans and one of the strongest entries in the Mortal Kombat series.

This WAS a very fun game until the online function randomly stopped working. I'm on Windows 10 but I had to reinstall the OS and after that, the online doesn't work anymore.

That's why I can't recommend this game. Its not a reliable purchase and I shouldn't have to mess with my computer's settings for the chance of it maybe working. But if you decide to try it and it works, there's a fun game in here. The moment to moment Kombat is really satisfying and crunchy, krushing blows are a neat mechanic and it looks gorgeous. I do miss the meter management from MKX though, I thought that made for more interesting matches.

As for the story, its the reboot timeline, now with time travel flavor. After this, M1K would go full multiverse. I don't like how the Mortal Kombat series is acting like a bad superhero comic. Its doesn't feel true to itself. I miss the atmosphere of the older games and the PS2 era, back when it was mysterious and creepy. Like a martial arts/horror game with a sense of humor. While there's a little of that here, its not the same. 

The Krypt (which doesn't work because no online access) is a fun little way to spend time and explore the world, though getting killed by monsters and traps is more annoying than anything. Same with the character customization. Fun feature but because the online doesn't work, good luck actually being able to use it. 

In the end, this game was always going to expire. Fighting games shouldn't be always online and this game is a textbook example why. Some of us just got to experience early what will happen to everyone when the servers eventually shut down. This game and the fans deserved better.
